Spring Boot · Java

Agents as plain interfaces

Declare what you need; the integration does the wiring.

  • Conversation history owned by the Copilot runtime
  • Spring beans exposed as Copilot tools
  • Local and remote MCP servers per agent
  • Micrometer metrics and Actuator health checks
Spring Boot documentation →
SpringAdvisor.java 
@CopilotAgent(
    name = "spring-advisor",
    instructions = "Explain Spring Boot concepts concisely.")
public interface SpringAdvisor {
    CompletableFuture<String> answer(
        @ConversationId String conversationId,
        @UserMessage String question);
}

The same patterns in every framework

The patterns from the Copilot SDK cookbook are built into each integration. Write configuration, not boilerplate.

  • Typed agents

    Declare an agent as an interface, decorated class, or subclass. The integration implements it and routes each call to the right conversation.

  • Your components as tools

    Spring and CDI beans, NestJS providers, .NET services, Django and FastAPI functions, and even Camel routes become tools, called with their normal DI, transactions, and security.

  • Deny-by-default permissions

    Tool use is denied unless you grant it. You can use declarative policies, allow-lists, and human-in-the-loop approvals; nothing is approved implicitly.

  • Conversations and sessions

    Create-or-resume per conversation ID, one turn at a time per session, and a session store that can list, read, and delete sessions. Age-based cleanup is opt-in.

  • MCP, BYOK, and tool search

    Local and remote MCP servers and your own model providers (OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, Anthropic, Ollama), set per agent. Large tool catalogs can be deferred behind runtime tool search.

  • Streaming and structured output

    Streams use the framework's own types (Mutiny, Reactor, RxJS, SSE, AI SDK useChat). Typed results come from records, zod schemas, and pydantic models.

  • Per-user identity

    Token resolvers authenticate each turn as the signed-in user, using Spring Security, Quarkus and Micronaut Security, Django auth, or your own resolver.

  • Observability and testing

    Micrometer, OpenTelemetry, framework health checks, and the Aspire dashboard. A scripted, in-memory runtime runs framework tests without consuming model usage.

  • Error-recovery hooks

    Opt-in hooks that tell the model to keep going after a failed tool call, with a limit on consecutive failures. Transient errors are retried in Python and Node.js.

  • Fresh-session loops

    A Ralph-loop runner that starts a fresh session on every iteration, with checks between iterations, stop conditions, timeouts, and cancellation.

  • Message provenance

    Label each prompt as user, system, or agent-<id>. Scheduled jobs and agent-to-agent calls are labeled automatically.

  • In-process runtime

    Java integrations can run the Copilot runtime inside the JVM instead of a child process. Startup checks the native dependencies and fails fast if any are missing.

Quarkus · Java

CDI beans as tools, streamed with Mutiny

Tools run through the bean's client proxy, so @Transactional and security interceptors still apply.

  • Agents discovered at build time and injected with @Inject
  • Multi<CopilotAgentEvent> streaming; cancelling the stream aborts the turn
  • SmallRye Health readiness, Micrometer timers, and a /q/copilot endpoint
  • @QuarkusTest with a scripted in-memory runtime
Quarkus documentation →
InventoryAgent.java 
@ApplicationScoped
@Named("inventoryTools")
public class InventoryTools {
    @Inject StockRepository stock;

    @Transactional
    @CopilotTool(value = "Count units in stock", name = "check_stock")
    public long checkStock(@CopilotToolParam("SKU") String sku) {
        return stock.countBySku(sku);
    }
}

@CopilotAgent(name = "inventory",
        instructions = "Answer stock questions using the tools.",
        toolRefs = "inventoryTools",
        permissionHandlerRef = "inventoryApprovals")
public interface InventoryAgent {
    Multi<CopilotAgentEvent> chat(@ConversationId String id,
                                  @UserMessage String question);
}
Micronaut · Java

Agent governance in configuration

Override any @CopilotAgent attribute per environment. The settings are validated at startup, so a missing tool bean or unknown MCP server stops the app from starting.

  • Agents registered at compile time, without reflection
  • Per-agent model, permissions, MCP servers, BYOK provider, and tool search
  • Experimental in-process runtime: no child process, with a fail-fast native check
  • Micronaut Security identity, health, /info, and Micrometer
Micronaut documentation →
application.properties 
# Run the Copilot runtime inside the JVM
micronaut.copilot.connection=inprocess

# Per-agent overrides of @CopilotAgent attributes
micronaut.copilot.agents.advisor.model=gpt-5.2-codex
micronaut.copilot.agents.advisor.permissions.allow=read
micronaut.copilot.agents.advisor.mcp-servers=github
micronaut.copilot.agents.advisor.provider=foundry
micronaut.copilot.agents.advisor.tool-search.defer-threshold=20

micronaut.copilot.mcp.servers.github.type=http
micronaut.copilot.mcp.servers.github.url=https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/

micronaut.copilot.providers.foundry.base-url=${FOUNDRY_URL}
micronaut.copilot.providers.foundry.api-key=${FOUNDRY_API_KEY}
Apache Camel · Java

Agents as route steps, routes as tools

A copilot: component that turns an agent into one more step in your integration flows.

  • Structured output into a POJO, then routed with Camel's own EIPs
  • One Copilot session per CopilotConversationId header
  • Any route can be a tool (SQL, REST, Kafka) behind agent permissions
  • Human-in-the-loop approvals and session events as Camel routes
Apache Camel documentation →
TriageRoutes.java 
from("kafka:tickets")
    .setHeader("CopilotConversationId", header("ticketId"))
    .to("copilot:agent:triage"
        + "?instructions=Classify the support ticket."
        + "&toolRefs=lookupOrder&allowAgentTools=true"
        + "&outputClass=com.acme.Triage")
    .choice()
        .when(simple("${body.severity} == 'HIGH'")).to("jira:create")
        .otherwise().to("log:triage");

from("copilot:tool:lookupOrder"
        + "?description=Look up an order by id"
        + "&parametersClass=com.acme.OrderQuery")
    .to("sql:select status from orders where id = :#${body.id()}"
        + "?outputType=SelectOne");
NestJS · TypeScript

Decorated agents with injectable tools

Agents are classes with decorators, and tools are ordinary providers that run on the DI instance.

  • @Returns(zod) for typed results, Observable for streams
  • Templates validated at bootstrap; tool interceptors and hooks as providers
  • Request-scoped identity and per-user MCP credentials
  • Terminus health, SSE, and an AI SDK adapter for useChat
NestJS documentation →
support.agent.ts 
@Injectable()
export class OrdersTools {
  constructor(private readonly orders: OrdersService) {}

  @CopilotTool({
    description: "Look up an order",
    input: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  })
  lookupOrder({ id }: { id: string }, invocation: CopilotToolInvocation) {
    return this.orders.find(id, invocation.context.principal);
  }
}

@CopilotAgent({
  name: "support",
  instructions: "You are a support agent.",
  tools: [OrdersTools],
  permissions: permissions.allowCustomTools(),
})
export abstract class SupportAgent {
  @UserMessage("Extract the order from: {{text}}")
  @Returns(Order)
  extract(@P("text") text: string): Promise<z.infer<typeof Order>> {
    return implementedByCopilot();
  }

  @UserMessage()
  chat(@ConversationId() id: string,
       @Message() q: string): Observable<CopilotAgentEvent> {
    return implementedByCopilot();
  }
}
Fastify · TypeScript

From plugin to chat UI in a few lines

Register the plugin once. Each request gets agents bound to the caller, and replies can stream as SSE or as the AI SDK UI message stream.

  • request.copilot.agent() is bound to the request's identity and abort signal
  • reply.copilotChat() serves useChat, including tool approvals
  • Typed agent names, health routes, and graceful shutdown
  • Opt-in age-based session cleanup
Fastify documentation →
server.ts 
const support = defineAgent({
  name: "support",
  model: "gpt-5",
  instructions: "You help customers.",
});

await app.register(copilotPlugin, {
  agents: [support],
  health: true,                         // GET /health/copilot
  sessionCleanup: { maxAge: WEEK_MS },  // delete idle sessions
});
await app.register(copilotAiPlugin);

// AI SDK useChat endpoint, with tool approvals
app.post("/api/chat", async (request, reply) =>
  reply.copilotChat({ agent: "support" }));

// Server-Sent Events
app.get("/stream", async (request, reply) =>
  reply.copilotEvents(
    request.copilot.agent("support").stream({ prompt: "Hi" })));
.NET · C#

Copilot behind IChatClient

Built on Microsoft.Extensions.AI. Inject IChatClient and the integration handles sessions, tools, and approvals.

  • DI services as tools, each call in its own DI scope with HttpContext intact
  • [RequiresApproval] tools go through OnApproval; everything else is denied
  • Typed results: GetResponseAsync<TicketTriage>(prompt)
  • Health checks, OpenTelemetry, and a CopilotLoopRunner
.NET documentation →
Program.cs 
builder.Services.AddCopilot(o =>
{
    o.Instructions = "You are Contoso's customer support assistant.";
    o.OnApproval = call =>
        ValueTask.FromResult(call.GetArgument<decimal>("amount") < 100);
}).WithTools<OrderTools>();         // DI service methods become tools

app.MapPost("/chat", async (IChatClient chat, ChatRequest req,
                            CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var response = await chat.GetResponseAsync(req.Message,
        new() { ConversationId = req.ConversationId }, ct);
    return new ChatReply(response.Text, response.ConversationId);
});
Aspire · Polyglot

The Copilot runtime as an AppHost resource

Aspire runs the runtime, manages its secrets and connection strings, and connects every service that references it.

  • One WithReference wires services in .NET, Java, Node.js, or Python
  • GitHub token as a secret parameter, with a generated connection token
  • End-to-end traces on the dashboard: request → turn → model → tool
  • MCP servers and BYOK providers referenced from other resources
Aspire documentation →
AppHost.cs 
var copilot = builder.AddCopilot("copilot");  // headless runtime
var chat    = copilot.AddModel("chat", "gpt-5.4");

builder.AddProject<Projects.Api>("api")
       .WithReference(chat)
       .WaitFor(chat);
Api/Program.cs 
builder.AddCopilotClient("chat",
           o => o.Instructions = "You help customers with orders.")
       .WithTools<OrderTools>();

app.MapPost("/ask", async (IChatClient chat, string q) =>
    (await chat.GetResponseAsync(q)).Text);
Django · Python

ORM-aware tools with Django permissions

Tools check user.has_perm, can run in transaction.atomic, and only see the current user's data.

  • @prompt methods typed by their return annotation (str or pydantic)
  • Conversations partitioned per user, so users can't resume each other's sessions
  • System checks, a copilot_check command, and session cleanup for cron
  • Autodiscovered copilot_tools and copilot_agents modules
Django documentation →
shop/copilot_agents.py 
@copilot_tool
def lookup_order(order_id: int, ctx: ToolContext) -> dict:
    """Look up one of the current user's orders."""
    order = Order.objects.get(pk=order_id, owner=ctx.user)
    return {"id": order.pk, "status": order.status}

@copilot_tool(permission_required="shop.refund_order", atomic=True)
def refund_order(order_id: int, ctx: ToolContext) -> str:
    """Refund an order."""
    ...

class SupportAgent(CopilotAgent):
    instructions = "You are a support agent. Be concise."
    tools = [lookup_order, refund_order]
    permissions = policies.allow_registered_tools()

    @prompt("Should order {{ order_id }} be refunded? "
            "Reason given: {{ reason }}")
    def decide_refund(self, order_id: int, reason: str) -> Decision: ...
FastAPI · Python

Agents injected with Depends

Agents are dependencies. Their tools see the current user and anything you inject, such as a database session.

  • Typed @prompt methods returning pydantic models
  • HTTPException in a tool becomes the message the model sees
  • pydantic-settings configuration with validation in the app's lifespan
  • GET /copilot/health and a scripted test runtime
FastAPI documentation →
app/main.py 
copilot = Copilot(agents=[SupportAgent], current_user=get_current_user)
app = FastAPI(lifespan=copilot.lifespan,
              exception_handlers=copilot.exception_handlers)
app.include_router(copilot.router())        # GET /copilot/health

Support = Annotated[
    SupportAgent, copilot.depends(SupportAgent, db=Depends(get_db))
]


@app.get("/orders/{order_id}/status")
async def status(order_id: int, agent: Support) -> dict:
    return {"answer": await agent.where_is(order_id)}


@app.post("/chat/{conversation_id}")
async def chat(conversation_id: str, message: str, agent: Support):
    reply = await agent.conversation(conversation_id).asend(message)
    return {"answer": reply}
